about: A rearranged Zork: the white house, the kitchen window, the trophy case, and a cellar that opens straight onto the troll. From there the dam, the maintenance room and the Loud Room are a short walk away. It's a treasure-and-puzzle trek through the familiar Great Underground Empire, with the map shuffled.

done.why: I had seen the shuffled route and the main set pieces, and I had the platinum bar. Nothing pulled me further, and no ending was in sight.

moments.note: The cellar leads straight to the troll room, and the sword glows brighter as you go.
The troll fell in two blows, and the sinister fog line from the original is kept.
The bolt description says its flats are worn bright, the way bolts get when only a wrench turns them. It quietly hints at the solution.
The Loud Room echoes 'bar bar ...' when you try to take the bar, and 'echo' changes the acoustics.
Going east from North of House led to Behind House, which is a rearranged map.

wished: More to examine in the rooms, such as the dam and the troll room.
A clearer sense of what the goal is.

lines.line: Its flats are worn bright, the way bolts get when the only way to turn them is with a wrench.
painted to match the house and a good deal less weathered
lines.why: The mailbox is described with a dry, specific wit.

lines.line: The stream is clear and cold and in no particular hurry
lines.why: A good line of new prose, fitting the original's tone.

fun.why: Quick, satisfying progress and clever touches like the echo room.

engagement.why: Compact route, but little reason to linger once the layout is clear.

difficulty.why: Mostly easy and forgiving. The item limit was the only snag.

interestingness.why: The remixed geography keeps you from playing from memory.

prose.why: The original is mixed with new descriptions that are well written and distinctive.
